_README: LAB ONLY. Consumed by examples/ticket_lab_authority.py, which makes the
gateway an authority on what tickets are worth. Delete both when the
bench work is finished.
COPY THIS TO lab_tickets.json AND PUT YOUR REAL NUMBERS THERE.
lab_tickets.json is gitignored. The numbers below are placeholders:
a validation number identifies a real ticket issued by a real property,
so it is operational data and does not belong in a repository.
The keys are the numbers printed on the tickets; dashes are optional.
The printed value, date and issuing property are all irrelevant -- the
machine reads the barcode for a validation number and nothing else, so
already-redeemed tickets from a decommissioned system are fine as test
media. 'as' and 'amount' here are what the ticket is worth.
machine_serial binds the file to one cabinet. The tool reads the serial
and refuses to run against any other, so these tickets cannot be
honoured somewhere they were never meant to be.
machine_asset is the FALLBACK, and on some cabinets it is the only
binding that works: section 4.4 lets a machine ignore LP 0x54 and this
project's own lab EGM does, so a serial-only binding cannot be checked
against it at all and the run refuses to start. Set machine_asset to the
number on the cabinet's asset tag and the binding becomes enforceable.
Where both are present the SERIAL decides: it is burned in and survives
a RAM clear, while an asset number is typed in and a clear wipes it, so
a matching serial is not vetoed by an asset that was retyped. The asset
is compared only when the serial cannot be read at all. Set either, or
both; a file with neither will redeem against any cabinet and says so.
machine_asset must be a number. The SAS field is a 4-byte binary
integer, so a letter cannot appear in it. Zero is the field's unset
value rather than an asset number, and is rejected.
